name.text: Finding the mistake in a model

questiontext.text:
{@E[1]@}

  • {@E[2][1]@}
  • {@E[2][2]@}
  • {@E[2][3]@}

Wambui wrote this model, with \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\):

(1) \({@E[7][1]@}\)    (2) \({@E[7][2]@}\)    (3) \({@E[7][3]@}\)

Each inequality (1) to (3) is meant to match the sentence in the same place. One of them does not match its sentence.

(a) Which one?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Write it correctly.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The correct model is (1) \({@E[8][1]@}\), (2) \({@E[8][2]@}\), (3) \({@E[8][3]@}\).

Wambui's inequality ({@kk@}) is \({@wk@}\), which does not match its sentence: it should be \({@E[8][kk]@}\). Read each sentence for its key words (at most \(\le\), at least \(\ge\), more than \(\gt\), fewer than \(\lt\)), check which letter each number belongs to, and check a ‘times as many’ sentence with numbers.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: finding the mistake in a model

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (a) / Essential 1.4 (a): Read three conditions and a model of them, find the inequality that does not match its sentence, and correct it.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: ch: if ans1 = "i1" then 1 elseif ans1 = "i2" then 2 elseif ans1 = "i3" then 3 else 1;

truefeedback.text: One inequality does not match: read each sentence again and check the sign, the letters and the numbers.

falsefeedback.text: Inequality ({@ch@}) matches its sentence: it is \({@E[8][ch]@}\). Look at the others.

feedbackvariables.text: c2: lcls(ans2, tk); w2: lcls(ans2, wk); ds: is(c2 = "dir" or c2 = "strict");

truefeedback.text: That is Wambui's inequality, which is the one with the mistake.

[[if test='is(c2="dir")']]

The boundary is right but the side is wrong: your inequality allows what sentence ({@kk@}) rules out. Test a pair of numbers that fits the sentence.

[[else]]

The side is right, but the words in sentence ({@kk@}) {@incl@} the number at the boundary.

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Write the sentence for inequality ({@kk@}) again, word by word.

qtest.description: Wrong index; side or strictness changed (not Wambui's)
